work.title: Plato, Phaedo
work.notes: Plato's narrated dialogue about Socrates' final day. Its developed metaphysics of soul and Forms may reflect Plato's philosophy and must not be treated as a transparent transcript of the historical Socrates.

edition.label: Benjamin Jowett English translation; Project Gutenberg #1658
edition.licenseNote: Project Gutenberg metadata states public domain in the USA; verify the law of the deployment jurisdiction before production redistribution. Jowett's historical translation should be checked against the Greek for precise terminology.

passages.translationText: And the true philosophers, Simmias, are always occupied in the practice of dying, wherefore also to them least of all men is death terrible.
passages.interpretiveNote: In the dialogue, “practice of dying” concerns philosophical separation from bodily distractions and preparation for death within Plato's argument about the soul. It is not advocacy of self-harm, and the developed doctrine is not secure evidence for the historical Socrates.
passages.period: Platonic representation with developed metaphysics; historical English translation
